content: Pro-Mode Search Parser: A full recursive-descent parser was introduced that compiles rich boolean search expressions directly into PostgreSQL tsquery. The parser implements a formal grammar (AND, OR, NOT, FOLLOWED_BY with the adjacency proximity operator and configurable distance operator, plus parenthesized grouping) via a multi-pass AST pipeline: lexing (ProQueryLexer tokenizing commands like G (geographic scope), LOC (location), R (radius), Y (year) with colon-colon delimiters, plus the AND, OR, and NOT operators), parsing (ProQueryParser with precedence-ordered parseOr, parseAnd, parseComparison, parseFollowedBy, parseUnary, and parsePrimary phases), semantic expansion (CommandExpansionPass resolving taxonomic and geographic commands against the database and SPARQL endpoint, TaxonEnrichmentPass enriching plain taxon terms with alternative names from the knowledge graph), AST normalization (deduplication and canonical ordering), and finally tsquery compilation (ProTsQueryCompiler generating PostgreSQL tsquery strings with proper AND conjunction, OR disjunction, NOT negation, adjacency proximity, and distance N syntax). The backend passes proModeActivated=true through the search flow (SearchApi to EnrichedSearchQuery to Search_DefaultImpl to PostgresqlDataInterface) so that the database layer applies to_tsquery with the simple dictionary configuration to preserve operator semantics. Frontend delivers a chip-based visual query builder (proModeSearchBar FreeMarker template, JavaScript, and CSS) with inline editing, command indicators, grouping overlays, and real-time syntax error display fed from ProModeSyntaxException diagnostics. The entire parser is backed by unit tests (ProQueryParserTest) covering expression compilation and error reporting.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: DUUI Importer Pipeline Architecture: The corpus import system was migrated from a legacy CompletableFuture-based batch processor to a staged DUUI pipeline framework. The new pipeline implements a typed document processing graph: a RuntimeSeedGenerator feeds into CorpusToDocuments fork, followed by sequential pipeline stages — document-read (wait-for-batch), document-jcas (open-document-jcas, annotate-gnfinder-podman, initialize-document-shell), parallel document-independent-extraction (UCE metadata, sentences, NER, sentiments, emotions, lemmata, SRL, times, taxonomy, wikilinks, negation, topics, images, permissions all executing concurrently), document-dependent-extraction (geonames, pages, logical-links), document-domain-capture (domain graph recording via AgeGraphService), document-persist (persist-document, persist-domain-association-graph), document-post (post-process-document-and-batch), and finally corpus-finalize (refresh logical links, lexicon, geonames, postprocess, persist operation graph). A DUUI-as-a-service variant (DUUICorpusImporter) wraps this pipeline behind HTTP endpoints implementing the DUUI protocol (at paths for communication layer, type system, process, and input/output details) for integration with external DUUI orchestration. Concurrency robustness was added to all services (PostgresqlDataInterface, AgeGraphService, S3StorageService, JenaSparqlService, LexiconService, EmbeddingService) to handle parallel pipeline stages safely.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: Importer Connection Pooling and Service Resilience: The import pipeline's database access layer was hardened with HikariCP connection pooling configured through Hibernate (HibernateConf wiring through CommonConfig properties). Pool sizing (maximum 10 connections, minimum 2 idle) with configurable connection timeout (30s), idle timeout (10min), max lifetime (30min), and leak detection threshold (60s) prevents connection exhaustion during parallel pipeline stages. The architecture enforces a strict separation of concerns: pipeline stages define import semantics only and do not own service pool management — each service (PostgresqlDataInterface, AgeGraphService, S3StorageService, JenaSparqlService, LexiconService, EmbeddingService) is responsible for its own capacity, blocking behavior, and retry logic. Safe tsquery SQL functions were designed (15_safe_tsquery_functions.sql) with array-to-tsquery escaping, term length limits, and automatic fallback to plainto_tsquery on overflow. An enhanced two-phase search function (16_enhanced_search_function.sql) chunks large expanded term sets into batches of 50 terms, executes a first-phase query, and only fans out to additional chunked queries if insufficient results are returned, avoiding giant tsquery strings that would degrade PostgreSQL GIN index performance.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: Importer Pipelined Processing with Configurable Parallelism: The importer was restructured to support configurable thread-level parallelism (via the numThreads command-line flag) that controls DUUI document task concurrency independently of service pool capacity. Input handling was extended to support .xmi, .bz2, .zip, and .gz corpus formats with automatic decompression. The import flow produces S3-stored raw XMI backups when enableS3Storage is set, and executes post-processing continuations (embedding generation, topic modeling, batch management) through DocumentImportContinuation. An importer harness test framework was added with podman-compose orchestration for local profiling, correctness matrix testing across domain subsets, service health checking, and Jupyter-based import profiling notebooks for performance analysis.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: GNFinder Taxon Abbreviation Diagnostic: A diagnostic script scans imported UCE corpus XMI files for abbreviated gnfinder taxon annotations (e.g. 'C. muricata' where the genus is only an initial) that likely need repair. For each abbreviated gnfinder Taxon element found, the script identifies nearby fully-verified gnfinder VerifiedTaxon annotations by character offset proximity, infers the full genus from the nearest verified match starting with the same initial letter, and queries the GBIF species API (species match and species search endpoints) to obtain canonical expansion candidates with confidence scores and taxonomic status. The output is a JSONL manifest for human review before any XMI patching decision is made — the tool is intentionally conservative and never modifies corpus data. Supports compressed XMI input (.xmi, .xmi.gz, .xmi.bz2) and provides configurable file scan limits and GBIF request timeouts.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: FUSEKI GBIF Taxon Enrichment for RDF Patching: A generic taxon name enrichment tool queries the full GBIF taxonomic API surface to produce comprehensive JSON reports for comparison against Fuseki/TDB RDF store contents. For each input scientific name, the tool resolves exact homonym usages from GBIF species search (casefold-canonical matching), follows accepted usage chains via acceptedKey resolution (handling synonyms pointing to their accepted names), and collects full taxonomic context: all synonyms, subordinate taxa (subspecies, variety, form, and forma only), and vernacular names across multiple languages. The output is a structured report per query with sections for GBIF match diagnostics, exact canonical usages, accepted usage summaries, source-to-accepted mappings, and a deduplicated expansionNames list usable for RDF patching decisions. Uses LRU-cached HTTP fetches to avoid redundant GBIF API calls when the same taxon key appears in multiple contexts. Designed as a read-only diagnostic — never modifies Fuseki data, only produces comparison artifacts for human review.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: Layered Search with Dirty-Layer Tracking and Geographic Queries: A materialized-view-based layered search system was implemented that decomposes complex multi-faceted queries into independently computed layers. Each search layer materializes results into the PostgreSQL search schema (tables named with the pattern layered_search followed by identifier and depth) supporting TAXON, TIME, and LOCATION slot types with command-driven expansion. Geographic layers leverage PostGIS ST_DWithin for radius-based spatial queries. The system tracks layer dirtiness — only re-executing layers whose parameters changed since the last computation — avoiding redundant work across incremental query refinements. All materialized tables are cleaned up via dropAllTables() on disposal, preventing schema pollution. The layered search builder frontend (layered-search-builder CSS and JavaScript) integrates with the pro-mode parser to compose slot-aware queries.
author: Dawit Terefe

content: Podman Compose Deployment and Profile-Based Service Orchestration: A Podman-compatible compose file (podman-compose.yaml) was added alongside helper scripts (install-podman-ubuntu.sh, podman-compose-up.sh) enabling rootless container deployment as an alternative to Docker. A new 'web' Compose profile was introduced allowing the UCE web application to be started standalone without authentication dependencies. The SPARQL_HOST environment variable was propagated into the uce-web container to support container-network-resolved Fuseki endpoints. The deployment configuration now supports SSH-tunneled database connectivity via an alpine-based SSH tunnel container with automatic reconnection, enabling UCE to operate against remote PostgreSQL instances through a bastion host.
author: Dawit Terefe
